t:
(a) Prohibition on Use of SCHIP Funds.—Section 2107 of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1397gg) is amended by adding at the end the following:“(f) Limitation of Waiver Authority.—Notwithstanding subsection (e)(2)(A) and section 1115(a), the Secretary may not approve a waiver, experimental, pilot, or demonstration project that would allow funds made available under this title to be used to provide child health assistance or other health benefits coverage to a nonpregnant childless adult. For purposes of the preceding sentence, a caretaker relative (as such term is defined for purposes of carrying out section 1931) shall not be considered a childless adult.”.  
    (b) Conforming Amendments.—Section 2105(c)(1) of such Act (42 U.S.C. 1397ee(c)(1)) is amended—
        (1) by inserting “and may not include coverage of a nonpregnant childless adult” after “section 2101)”; and 
        (2) by adding at the end the following: “For purposes of the preceding sentence, a caretaker relative (as such term is defined for purposes of carrying out section 1931) shall not be considered a childless adult.”.   
    (c) Rule of Construction.—Nothing in this section or the amendments made by this section shall be construed to—
        (1) authorize the waiver of any provision of title XIX or XXI of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1396 et seq., 1397aa et seq.) that is not otherwise authorized to be waived under such titles or under title XI of such Act (42 U.S.C. 1301 et seq.) as of the date of enactment of this Act; 
        (2) imply congressional approval of any waiver, experimental, pilot, or demonstration project affecting funds made available under the State children’s health insurance program under title XXI of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1397aa et. seq.) or any amendment to such a waiver or project that has been approved as of such date of enactment; or 
        (3) apply to any waiver, experimental, pilot, or demonstration project that would allow funds made available under title XXI of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1397aa et seq.) to be used to provide child health assistance or other health benefits coverage to a nonpregnant childless adult that is 
approved before the date of enactment of this Act or to any extension, renewal, or amendment of such a waiver or project that is approved on or after such date of enactment.  
    (d) Effective Date.—This section and the amendments made by this section shall take effect as if enacted on October 1, 2005, and shall apply to any waiver, experimental, pilot, or demonstration project that is approved on or after that date.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that state waiver or demonstration projects involve states interacting with the federal Secretary, but a waiver request is an application for approval, not consultation on a federal decision. The section only restricts the Secretary's authority to approve such waivers and sets rules of construction and an effective date. It creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation requirement, rulemaking mandate, or right to sue.
fable.s: the Secretary may not approve a waiver, experimental, pilot, or demonstration project that would allow funds made available under this title to be used to provide child health assistance or other health benefits coverage to a nonpregnant childless adult

opus.w: This section only limits the Secretary's power to approve SCHIP waivers covering childless adults, and adds conforming amendments, a rule of construction and an effective date. It creates no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue for anyone outside the federal government. A State asking for a waiver is an application for approval, not participation, and the reference to congressional approval stays inside the federal government.
opus.s: the Secretary may not approve a waiver, experimental, pilot, or demonstration project that would allow funds made available under this title to be used to provide child health assistance or other health benefits coverage to a nonpregnant childless adult.
opus.b:
1. **Tempting reading:** States ask the Secretary to approve waiver and demonstration projects, so an outside party (a State) seems to take part in a federal decision. That fails against the definition. Asking for a waiver is an application for approval or benefits, which the definition excludes. The section also only limits what the Secretary may approve. It requires no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue. The mention of "congressional approval" in (c)(2) concerns Congress, which is inside the federal government.

qwen_chat.w: This section imposes a substantive prohibition on the Secretary's authority to approve certain waivers. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation with outside parties (such as states, tribes, or the public) in the decision-making process. The definition excludes applications for benefits or grants, and this text merely limits the scope of allowable waivers without describing a participatory process.
qwen_chat.s: the Secretary may not approve a waiver, experimental, pilot, or demonstration project that would allow funds made available under this title to be used to provide child health assistance or other health benefits coverage to a nonpregnant childless adult.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the mention of "waiver, experimental, pilot, or demonstration project" implies a process where states or other entities apply for waivers, which could involve consultation. However, the text itself only prohibits the Secretary from approving certain types of waivers; it does not describe the process for applying for or consulting on those waivers. The definition explicitly excludes "applications for benefits or grants" and requires that the section itself involve consultation or coordination with outside parties. This section is a substantive prohibition on the use of funds, not a procedural requirement for participation.
